cells.tense: You're here with it now, and the pen's in your hand.
cells.verb: Choosing one real connection and letting the two of you become one stream
cells.place: at the threshold where what's arriving comes in from outside
cells.ask: Offer the next step toward that person from what you actually feel, not from what sounds right — and let the direction that comes back prove itself by moving you.
cells.core:
A real connection is being chosen right now, and you're the one choosing it. Two streams met and decided to run together — that decision is the whole event, and it's happening because you can see where it's going, not because it was easy. What arrives next comes in through that door, not around it.

The sure-footedness you feel isn't a pause before the real work. It's the wave you're riding.
cells.sheetLine: You're choosing this connection on purpose, and you know where it's headed.

cells.tense: You're already living a version of this that hasn't arrived.
cells.verb: Merging ahead of the meeting — closing a connection that hasn't happened yet
cells.place: at the door, before what's entering has entered
cells.ask: Let one thing grow at the pace it's actually growing — tend what's here instead of what you're bracing for, and notice that the care doesn't have to exhaust you to count.
cells.core:
You've already decided how this goes. The person hasn't finished arriving, the moment hasn't finished opening, and you're three moves into a future you wrote alone. The force you're putting into the connection is the connection's biggest threat — you're pressing two streams together instead of letting them meet.

What's waiting on the other side of this isn't more of your effort. It's the thing your effort is crowding out.
cells.sheetLine: You've merged with a future that hasn't shown up yet.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door you already walked past.
cells.verb: Not merging — holding the connection at the threshold
cells.place: at the entrance where what's arriving goes unrecognized
cells.ask: Say what you actually perceive about one person, once, without arguing for it — and let being read correctly do the work your hesitation keeps overriding.
cells.core:
Something genuine is here, at the door, and you've been calling it undecided. The meeting keeps offering itself and you keep not quite showing up to it — not refusing, just not arriving. You know more about this connection than you're willing to stand behind, so you stay on the near side, waiting for certainty you already have.

What's missing isn't another sign. It's letting yourself be seen knowing what you know.
cells.sheetLine: The connection is here. You're still on the other side of the door.

cells.tense: The pen's down, but the page is already filling.
cells.verb: Shaping what arrives by how you meet it — while calling it just how things are
cells.place: at the moment something enters, where timing isn't being named
cells.ask: Give one arriving thing an actual hour of your attention this week — a small steady practice, nothing forced — and let the direction it reveals be yours instead of something you waited for.
cells.core:
You're already the one deciding what gets in and how it's met. Somebody has to be, and it's been you — the result of how you show up keeps coming out with your handwriting on it, and you keep describing it as the situation. The choosing is running. The knowing-you're-choosing it isn't.

What's in front of you was never waiting for a verdict to announce itself. It was waiting for you to notice it was already in.
cells.sheetLine: You're already deciding what enters and how. You just haven't said so.
